extra.message: Incoming WebSocket chatMessage.author.name and chatMessage.message are concatenated into p.innerHTML and appended to the document without sanitization. When the recipient has the sender's chat open, a message containing HTML such as an image with an onerror handler executes JavaScript in the recipient's application origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: showContactDetails passes user.emailAddress from the user API directly to jQuery replaceWith(), which interprets strings as HTML. An attacker-controlled emailAddress containing executable markup runs JavaScript when another user clicks 'Click to show contact'. The email address is a user-supplied registration field, and this rendering path performs no sanitization. See [jQuery replaceWith documentation](https://api.jquery.com/replaceWith/).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Both backend base URLs use unencrypted HTTP to a public IP address. Login.js sends usernames and passwords to this address, Register.js sends passwords and email addresses, and Users.js exchanges private chat data through these URLs. When these requests are permitted, a network attacker can read credentials and messages and modify responses.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The user-controlled profile website opens with target="_blank" without rel="noopener" or rel="noreferrer". In browsers that do not implicitly apply noopener, an attacker-controlled destination retains window.opener and can redirect the original application tab to a phishing page. This finding is limited to those browsers; modern browsers generally provide implicit protection. See [MDN anchor documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/a).

cwe: CWE-1022: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access

extra.message: The complete private chat history returned by messages/chat is written to the browser console. Line 50 also logs each incoming message and its author. These unconditional logs expose private conversation content to anyone or any diagnostic tooling with access to console output.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
